papers.title: Accurate, Interdisciplinary and Transparent Structure-property Understanding with Deep Native Structural Reasoning

summary.tldr: SciReasoner is a multimodal scientific foundation model that unifies structural representations for proteins, small molecules, and inorganic crystals, achieving state-of-the-art performance across 86 benchmarks.
key_points: SciReasoner discretizes coordinates, topologies, and periodic connectivities into a unified structure-aware vocabulary, treating structural tokens as addressable evidence units.
In homology-controlled Gene Ontology prediction, SciReasoner increased F_max from 0.42 to 0.55 for Cellular Component annotation of low-homology and orphan-like proteins.
In chemistry, SciReasoner improved single-step retrosynthesis accuracy from 0.63 to 0.72, generating fragment-level disconnection and precursor-verification traces.
In materials science, its representations separate elemental and compound phases and resolve high- and low-band-gap regimes.
SciReasoner achieved state-of-the-art performance on 67 out of 86 benchmarks, with its reasoning traces preferred or comparable to a frontier large language model in 98% of cases.
summary.why_it_matters: This model provides a unified approach for interpretable structure-property understanding across biology, chemistry, and materials science, enhancing predictive accuracy and scientific inference.

papers.title: Scaling Mixture-of-Experts Video Pretraining for Embodied Intelligence

summary.tldr: LingBot-Video is a DiT-based, Mixture-of-Experts video pretraining paradigm tailored for embodied intelligence, using robot-oriented data and a multi-dimensional reward system.
key_points: Adopts a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture for improved modeling capacity and inference efficiency, scaled from scratch.
Utilizes a data profiling engine to augment internet videos with robot-oriented footage (manipulation, navigation, egocentric) for understanding actions and world dynamics.
Develops a multi-dimensional reward system to enforce alignment with physical rationality and task completion, beyond standard aesthetic or motion consistency criteria.
LingBot-Video is presented as an open-source MoE video foundation model for embodied intelligence.
summary.why_it_matters: This work aims to bridge the gap between digital video generation and physical robotic actuation by creating a video foundation model optimized for embodied intelligence.

papers.title: Dual Latent Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation

summary.tldr: LaMem-VLA introduces a latent-memory-native framework for Vision-Language-Action models, reconstructing historical experience into latent memory tokens to interweave with VLA reasoning for long-horizon tasks.
key_points: LaMem-VLA addresses VLA models' struggle with long-horizon, temporally dependent tasks by integrating historical experience directly into the latent embedding space.
The framework includes a curator to organize historical experience into short-term and long-term memory vaults.
A seeker queries these vaults for context-relevant evidence, which a condenser reconstructs into compact latent memory tokens.
A weaver injects these memory tokens with current observation and instruction into a continuous embedding sequence for VLA reasoning.
LaMem-VLA represents, retrieves, and consumes historical experience entirely within the continuous latent space, enabling memory to guide action generation.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach improves VLA model performance on complex, long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks by enabling fluid integration of historical context.

papers.title: Infinite Worlds with Versatile Interactions

summary.tldr: LingBot-World 2.0 introduces unbounded interaction, real-time distillation for 60 fps 720p video, diverse actions, and an agentic harness for world modeling, with a 14B model and a 1.3B lightweight counterpart.
key_points: Achieves unbounded interaction horizon with consistent output quality via a causal pretraining paradigm.
Guarantees rapid response time, sufficient for 720p video streams at 60 fps, through distillation of a real-time variant.
Introduces diverse interactive elements including attacking, archery, spell-casting, shooting, and richer text-driven events.
Integrates an agentic harness with a pilot agent for character behaviors and a director agent for synthesizing novel environmental elements.
Pairs a primary 14B model with a lightweight 1.3B counterpart for single GPU deployment and supports multi-player interaction.
summary.why_it_matters: This system enables more complex, dynamic, and accessible interactive world simulations for users.

papers.title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: SAO introduces single-rollout asynchronous optimization with token-level clipping and value-model training to improve stability and effectiveness in agentic reinforcement learning for LLMs.
key_points: SAO replaces group-wise sampling with single-rollout sampling (one rollout per prompt) to reduce off-policy effects and improve generalization in asynchronous RL.
Practical value-model training designs are incorporated to enhance the single-rollout strategy.
A strict double-side token-level clipping strategy is introduced to improve optimization stability.
SAO consistently outperforms GRPO and its variants on agentic coding and reasoning benchmarks like SWE-Bench Verified, BeyondAIME, and IMOAnswerBench.
SAO was deployed in the agentic RL pipeline for training the open GLM-5.2 model (750B-A40B).
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more stable and effective asynchronous reinforcement learning for large language models, particularly in long-horizon agentic tasks and online learning settings.

papers.title: RoboDojo: A Unified Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Comprehensive Evaluation of Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies

summary.tldr: RoboDojo is a unified sim-and-real benchmark with 42 simulation and 18 real-world tasks for comprehensive evaluation of generalist robot manipulation policies, supporting scalable and reproducible assessment.
key_points: RoboDojo includes 42 simulation tasks evaluating generalization, memory, precision, long-horizon execution, and open-vocabulary instruction following.
The benchmark features 18 real-world tasks designed to test policies under challenging physical deployment conditions.
Scalable evaluation is enabled through heterogeneous parallel simulation in Isaac Sim and a reproducible real-world system, RoboDojo-RealEval, with remote cloud access and standardized hardware.
XPolicyLab allows policies to be integrated once for evaluation across both simulation and real-world settings with minimal adaptation.
30 policies have been integrated into XPolicyLab and evaluated on RoboDojo, establishing a public leaderboard.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a standardized, comprehensive, and reproducible method for evaluating generalist robot manipulation policies across diverse capabilities and environments, accelerating development and comparison.

papers.title: WildCity: A Real-World City-Scale Testbed for Rendering, Simulation, and Spatial Intelligence

summary.tldr: WildCity is a new real-world multimodal dataset collected by autonomous fleets, featuring 18 trajectories averaging 83.7 km, designed to enable city-scale spatial AI and digital twin development.
key_points: WildCity dataset comprises 18 trajectories, each averaging 83.7 kilometers, capturing real-world urban perception challenges like dynamic objects and lighting variations.
The dataset supports an urban-tailored reconstruction baseline, converting reconstructed environments into a closed-loop simulator.
The project analyzes key challenges for urban digital twins: scalability, extrapolation, and uncertainty.
WildCity aims to advance city-scale rendering and AI spatial reasoning comparable to human cognition.
summary.why_it_matters: This dataset and testbed provide crucial data and tools for developing AI capable of perceiving and reasoning across entire cities, addressing a current limitation in foundation models.

papers.title: Sparse Delta Memory: Scaling the State of Linear RNNs through Sparsity

summary.tldr: Sparse Delta Memory (SDM) scales linear RNN hidden states to higher capacity using sparse addressing, improving long-context recall and in-context learning under isoFLOP constraints.
key_points: SDM extends Gated DeltaNet by replacing the dense key-value outer product with sparse reads and writes to a large explicit memory.
SDM achieves orders of magnitude higher hidden state capacity in gated linear RNNs.
Under an isoFLOP constraint and identical parameters, higher state memory capacity significantly improves in-context learning and long-context retrieval.
Learning the initial state of SDM memory as a parametric memory further improves performance on common-knowledge and reasoning tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach allows linear RNNs to overcome their state size limitations, improving performance on long-context tasks without increasing computational cost.

papers.title: Automating the Design of Embodied Agent Architectures

summary.tldr: This paper introduces AgentCanvas and KDLoop to systematically evaluate Agent Architecture Search (AAS) for perceptual embodied agents, demonstrating deployable success-rate gains and identifying unique challenges compared to text-domain AAS.
key_points: AgentCanvas is a typed-graph runtime for embodied executors, supporting editable node-and-wire programs with simulator-aware execution and episode-level logs.
KDLoop is a coding-agent search procedure that cycles through proposal, critique, experiment, and distillation, with triggered reflection after stalls, used for Agent Architecture Search.
Three AAS variants were evaluated across four embodied executors covering vision-language navigation, embodied question answering, and language-conditioned manipulation.

Architecture-level search yielded deployable and directional success-rate gains on embodied tasks, but also revealed issues like masked optimization signals due to rollout noise and local edit basin traps.
One high-scoring candidate was rejected due to a leak, highlighting the need for careful validation in embodied AAS.
summary.why_it_matters: Automating embodied agent architecture design can improve performance on complex tasks, but requires addressing specific challenges related to simulation noise and credit assignment.

papers.title: OPSD-V: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Post-Training Few-Step Autoregressive Video Generators

summary.tldr: OPSD-V is an on-policy self-distillation method for post-training few-step autoregressive video diffusion models, reducing long-horizon degradation while preserving inference speed.
key_points: OPSD-V uses real long-video data as temporal context during training to provide dense trajectory-level supervision.
The student model generates each video chunk conditioned on its own previously generated KV cache, mimicking inference-time rollout.
The teacher model is evaluated at the same denoising states as the student but uses an AR-consistent temporal cache where older history can be replaced by real-video context.
This provides dense denoising-level corrective targets under on-policy AR cache dynamics without altering the sampler, denoising steps, or inference-time cache mechanism.
Applied to Self-Forcing and LongLive models, OPSD-V shows improvements in visual quality, motion dynamics, and VBenchLong scores.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves the quality and motion dynamics of long videos generated by few-step autoregressive models, addressing a key limitation of existing approaches.

papers.title: AgentLens: Production-Assessed Trajectory Reviews for Coding Agent Evaluation

summary.tldr: AgentLens is a new benchmark for interactive code agents that evaluates entire trajectories, combining formal verification with LLM-written reviews and side-by-side comparisons to diagnose model behavior.
key_points: AgentLens evaluates the entire agent trajectory, including instruction following, tool use, self-verification, error recovery, and user interaction, rather than a single pass/fail metric.
The benchmark integrates formal verification for objective checks with LLM-written trajectory reviews.
AgentLens provides readable explanations for scores, enabling diagnosis of model behavior and comparison of agent versions.
It is used for catching product regressions in a nightly evaluation pipeline.
The benchmark is open-sourced at https://github.com/agent-lens/agent-lens-bench.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a more comprehensive and diagnostic evaluation for interactive code agents, moving beyond simple pass/fail to assess full operational trajectories.

papers.title: Teaching LLMs a Low-Resource Language: Enhancing Code Completion in Pharo

summary.tldr: This work demonstrates an end-to-end pipeline for bringing LLM-based code completion to low-resource languages like Pharo, showing specialized models outperform larger LLMs on Pharo completion benchmarks.
key_points: Developed an end-to-end pipeline for Pharo code completion, including data curation, continued pre-training, and fine-tuning of open code LLMs.
Introduced Pharo code completion benchmarks to evaluate syntax learning and accurate masked code completion from GitHub repositories.
Empirically showed Pharo-specialized models substantially outperform their original base checkpoints and larger code LLMs on Pharo completion tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables strong LLM-based code completion for low-resource programming languages with models suitable for real-time in-IDE support.

papers.title: RoboTALES: Learning Reasoning-Guided Robot Policies via Task-Aligned Simulated Futures

summary.tldr: RoboTALES introduces a single-stage framework for robot policies that uses a hierarchical LLM-based planner and a VLM-based critic to learn task-aligned simulated futures, improving temporal consistency and action coherence.
key_points: RoboTALES addresses video generative model limitations in visuomotor control by learning task-aligned simulated futures for robot policy training.
A hierarchical LLM-based planner guides the model's imagination by breaking complex tasks into subgoal sequences.
A VLM-based critic evaluates imagined futures and provides reward-based feedback to maintain goal-focused internal representations.
The method produces temporally consistent rollouts and coherent actions by anchoring the video generator in abstract reasoning.
RoboTALES outperforms existing methods on diverse manipulation tasks from RoboCasa and LIBERO10, particularly in long-horizon scenarios.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more reliable and coherent robot control for complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks by integrating reasoning into video generative models.

papers.title: Token-Based Dual-view Fusion and Adaptation of Large Vision Models for Breast Cancer Classification

summary.tldr: A token-centric dual-view learning framework unifies prompt-based adaptation and cross-view fusion within a frozen vision transformer backbone for breast cancer classification, improving upon existing multi-view methods.
key_points: The framework reformulates inter-view interaction as structured token-level communication using dedicated fusion tokens.
Fusion tokens explicitly encode bidirectional information exchange between CC and MLO views via cross-attention, acting as intermediate carriers.
Fusion modules are inserted at multiple transformer depths, enabling progressive and repeated interaction across the encoder hierarchy.
Fusion tokens are reintegrated into the token sequence and refined by subsequent transformer layers, preserving view-specific structure.
On VinDr-Mammo BI-RADS classification, the framework achieved 50.40% F1-score and 0.8090 AUC, with a 0.10 AUC improvement over a dual-view fusion baseline in the binary setting.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more effective way to integrate complementary mammography views, potentially leading to more accurate breast cancer diagnoses.

papers.title: TESSERA v2: Scaling Pixel-wise Earth Foundation Models

summary.tldr: TESSERA v2 presents a controlled scaling study for pixel-wise Earth-observation foundation models, identifying optimal pretraining strategies and achieving state-of-the-art performance with distilled models.
key_points: Conducted 395 training runs on 1,024 GH200 superchips within a fixed pixel-wise Barlow Twins family, evaluating on 15 downstream tasks.
Found pretraining loss poorly predicts downstream performance (|Pearson r| < 0.2), indicating model selection by loss wastes compute.
Determined that for increasing training budgets, encoder and data should scale together while the projector remains fixed.
The 21-million-parameter distilled TESSERA v2-1B-M outperforms all tested open and proprietary models, some orders of magnitude larger.
Distilled models produce Matryoshka representations, where a 16-dimensional prefix retains 92% of 128-dimensional performance at 1/8 storage.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides an empirically grounded methodology for efficiently scaling and deploying high-performing pixel-wise Earth-observation foundation models.

papers.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs

summary.tldr: This paper introduces correctness agreement to measure behavioral divergence in quantized LLMs, revealing significant changes even when accuracy and perplexity are preserved, and identifies sensitive attention projections.
key_points: Accuracy and perplexity metrics fail to capture behavioral changes in quantized LLMs.
Correctness agreement, a decision-level metric, measures overlap in correct predictions between base and quantized models.
Behavioral divergence emerges under moderate quantization (8-bit to 2-bit) despite preserved task performance.
Quantization acts as a structural operator on attention weights, with non-linear breakpoints at low bit-widths.
Query and key projections are consistently more sensitive to quantization than value and output projections.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying solely on accuracy and perplexity for quantized LLMs can mask significant behavioral changes, necessitating new evaluation metrics for reliable deployment.

papers.title: A Practical Investigation of Training-free Relaxed Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: This paper investigates training-free relaxed speculative decoding, unifying existing approaches and benchmarking them to provide practical findings for practitioners.
key_points: Relaxed speculative decoding sacrifices the strict sampling distribution guarantee of lossless methods for potential speed-ups, capability-speed trade-offs, or capability gains.
The investigation unifies existing relaxed speculative decoding techniques within a shared framework.
Benchmarking was conducted on contemporary settings to derive empirical findings.
Relaxation necessitates considerable capability evaluation, unlike lossless speculative decoding.
Many relaxed approaches require a drafter that functions as a good language model, making them unsuitable for lightweight multi-token-prediction drafters.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings provide practical guidance for implementing and evaluating relaxed speculative decoding in large language models.

papers.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing

summary.tldr: UltraX is a function-calling refinement framework for large-scale pre-training data, introducing insertion alongside deletion and modification for fine-grained instance-level editing.
key_points: UltraX expands the editing function space to include insertion, in addition to deletion and modification, for fine-grained instance-level editing.
It employs a program-supervision generation pipeline with dataset-adaptive prompt optimization to guide an expert LLM in producing refined texts.
Original-refined text pairs are converted into structured program supervision using Line Alignment Mapping and Dynamic Context Replacement.
Supervision quality is improved and training distribution stabilized via low-confidence example filtering and ratio-controlled sampling by operation combination.
Inference and execution involve sliding-window prediction, global operation aggregation, and systematic post-processing for stability and reliability.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves data quality and efficiency for LLM pre-training, addressing diminishing returns from data expansion.

papers.title: Cognitive-structured Multimodal Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Generation, and Editing

summary.tldr: A Cognitive-structured Multimodal Agent externalizes visual information into an Episodic Visual Memory, selectively reactivating relevant episodes to enable long-horizon multimodal dialogue and overcome visual token explosion.
key_points: The agent comprises a Perceptual Abstraction Engine for structured visual abstraction, a Cognitive Retrieval Engine for cross-turn memory retrieval, and a Multimodal Executive Controller for task inference and action planning.

A Unified Scenario Engine programmatically generates structured multi-turn conversations with fine-grained retrieval annotations to optimize abstraction and retrieval policies via reinforcement learning.
The 8B agent achieved 91.4% retrieval accuracy over 20-turn sessions, outperforming 32B baselines by 8.2% and reducing per-turn inference time from 23.1s to 12.7s.
The Cognitive-structured Multimodal Agent Harness (CMA-Harness) integrates persistent multimodal memory, web access, and image generation/editing/composition tools for deployment.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach offers a more scalable and efficient paradigm for long-horizon multimodal agents by addressing limitations of monolithic parameter scaling through structured memory and modular decision-making.

papers.title: Two Axes of LLM Abstention: Answer Correctness and Question Answerability

summary.tldr: LLMs exhibit distinct axes for answer correctness and question answerability; a two-axis abstention policy, using hidden state probes for answerability, significantly improves abstention performance over single-score methods.
key_points: Answer correctness and question answerability are separate axes for LLM abstention, not unified by a single confidence score.
Ordinary answer-confidence tracks correctness but is nearly blind to question answerability, especially for false-premise questions (CREPE dataset).
A linear probe on hidden states effectively detects question unanswerability, achieving 0.69 to 0.77 AUROC on false-premise questions, where other methods fail.
Instructing models to check premises directly backfires, leading to 57% false challenges; routing this instruction with the hidden-state probe roughly triples challenge precision.

A calibrated two-axis policy, using separate scores for answerability and correctness, certifies both unanswerable-answer and wrong-answer rates, achieving 0.75 coverage of correct answers compared to 0.31 for single-threshold policies.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more reliable LLM deployment by allowing precise control over abstention from incorrect answers and unanswerable questions, improving safety and trustworthiness.

papers.title: Game Theory Driven Multi-Agent Framework Mitigates Language Model Hallucination

summary.tldr: G-Frame, a multi-agent framework using Bayesian and game theory, synthesizes data and trains a 7B model, OmniChem, reducing hallucinations by 79.46% in scientific domains.
key_points: G-Frame employs an adaptive multi-agent framework integrating Bayesian and team game principles.
A specialized corpus of 363,045 chains-of-thought and 199,589 question-answer pairs was synthesized.
The 7B model, OmniChem, achieves performance parity with GPT 4o mini on custom benchmarks and ChemBench.
OmniChem demonstrates a 79.46% reduction in hallucinations compared to its base architecture.
OmniChem exhibits advanced capabilities in molecular design and synthesis planning.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a scalable method to mitigate reasoning deficiencies in lightweight LLMs for specialized scientific fields.

papers.title: Sensitivity-Aware Thresholding and Token Routing for Activation Sparsification in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: This paper introduces Sensitivity-Aware Thresholding for Sparsity (SATS) for layerwise gate threshold calibration and a token routing framework to improve activation sparsification in LLMs.
key_points: SATS calibrates layerwise gate thresholds using a local MLP output sensitivity proxy, replacing percentile-based calibration for activation sparsification.
A lightweight token routing framework dynamically selects between a base and modified computation path per-token, rather than applying modifications uniformly.
SATS improves over threshold-based sparsification baselines at matched actual sparsity.
Token routing yields a more favorable quality-throughput trade-off compared to static activation modification baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: These methods improve the quality-throughput trade-off for efficient inference in Large Language Models by optimizing activation sparsification and token-level conditional routing.

papers.title: Training, Reading, and Editing Legible Transformers

summary.tldr: This paper introduces a method to train legible transformers using bounded, named operators, achieving high legibility and editability without sacrificing quality.
key_points: A crispness penalty for legible operators can collapse them into dead constants due to its variance-minimizing nature, addressed by a per-channel variance floor.
A learned per-unit fraction replaces hand-set partitions, with the model routing 87% of computation through crisp operators.
The resulting transformer has 78% crisp-and-contextual detectors in feed-forward operands and 50% in attention value channels, with per-head legibility rising from 18% to 78% in deeper layers.
Edits to these crisp, sparse units are 50-184x more local in deep layers, enabling targeting explicit conjunctions.
A between-unit decorrelation pressure allows trading circuit reuse for independence, making concepts surgically editable units and predictions explainable.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more interpretable and directly editable transformer models, facilitating debugging and targeted modifications.

papers.title: Optimizing Against Safety Representations: Activation-Guided Adversarial Suffixes and the Geometry of Refusal

summary.tldr: This paper introduces Activation-Guided GCG and Soft-GCG to probe and attack internal safety representations in LLMs, finding distributed safety mechanisms and improved attack efficiency.
key_points: Activation-Guided GCG replaces output-based objectives with losses directly targeting a model's internal refusal direction.
Suppressing refusal globally across all layers and positions is more effective than targeting a single layer-position, indicating distributed safety representations.
Soft-GCG, a continuous relaxation using Gumbel-Softmax, achieves a 33x speedup over standard GCG while improving attack success rates.
Smaller models remain vulnerable to these attacks, while larger models resist both activation- and suffix-based attacks under compute constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how safety mechanisms are encoded and broken provides guidance for designing more robust and representation-aware alignment strategies for LLMs.

papers.title: How are linear representations learned? Exact solutions to the dynamics of abstraction

summary.tldr: This paper provides exact solutions for the dynamics of linear representation alignment (abstraction) during neural network training, revealing how data, target geometry, network depth, and initialization scale influence its emergence.
key_points: Exact solutions for abstraction trajectories in minimal linear networks show end-of-learning abstraction is determined by data and target geometry, improves with network depth, and its maximum is controlled by initialization scale.
In nonlinear networks, erf networks approximate linear theory, while ReLU networks' abstraction depends more on input geometry than target geometry.
A proven attenuation law states that both erf and ReLU nonlinearities weaken abstraction in activations compared to preactivations.
Evidence for the attenuation law is found in open models like DINOv3 and Gemma 4.
The theory is applied to improve linear probe generalization in LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding abstraction dynamics can improve interpretability and control methods in deep learning, such as linear probes and activation steering.
